newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian shares gain as results come out.
newsitem.headline: Latvian shares gain as results come out.

text.p: Latvia's bourse shook off its summer slumber on Thursday with shares rising in higher trade, leaving dealers optimistic about modest short-term gains as interim results begin to trickle out.
Overall market volume was up to 136,000 lats from 108,000 lats and the bourse index climbed 0.59 percent to 376.95. The Rietumu index gained to 150.34, up 0.64 percent.

Secondary list stock Jekabpils sugar led the risers for the second straight session as the market responded warmly to its interim results. It leapt to 65 santimes from 57 santimes on turnover of 5,800 lats.
"Its six-month profit of 400,000 lats was fantastic, far higher than expected," said one broker.
"The market is now waiting for other results from Riga Shipyard and The Riga Transport Fleet and they are expected to be good," said one dealer. "That should bring some short-term gains."
Riga Shipyard was well traded at 29,300 lats but unchanged at 1.36 lats.

Unibanka remained the focus of the market's attention, accounting for over half of the session's turnover in trade of 70,200 lats. It gained for the second straight day after a three-session slide, inching up to 3.15 lats from 3.13.
Dealers had expected it to fall to 3.05 lats, the minimum price announced by the privatisation agency for a July 28 auction of one million of the state's shares in the bank.
The market was divided over the reasons behind the rally, with some dealers speculating that someone was attempting to support the price and others saying that it still looks like a good buy.
